title: Autosuggest batching & cache profiles with traffic-aware limiters and anomaly-triggered rollback
creator: Aisha Rao
description:
Background:
We have multiple ongoing efforts that recommend batching and KV/prefix-caching configurations to reduce per-token cost. Past experiments show meaningful unit-cost improvements, but naive application can cause P95/P99 latency regressions under certain traffic shapes (short sessions, high concurrency) or amplify tail behavior when combined with autoscaling.

Goal:
Build an end-to-end Autosuggest pipeline that generates safe batching/cache profiles per route and applies them with runtime guardrails so that cost wins are realized without violating latency/throughput SLOs. The system should: suggest candidate profiles; verify them in shadow and canary modes; enforce runtime limiters during rollout; detect anomalies quickly; and automatically rollback or degrade safely when SLOs are threatened.

Non-goals:
- Replace manual tuning for very-high-risk enterprise routes on first pass.
- Optimize for absolute lowest cost irrespective of latency.

Acceptance criteria (must be testable):
1) A/B or canary apply can be executed for a route with a suggested profile and the control plane records the experiment and affected node set.
2) If a candidate profile is applied to 10% of traffic for 1 hour, monitored metrics must show: p99 latency regression < 2% for the route OR automated rollback triggers.
3) System provides rollback actions: immediate revert to baseline config, reduce batch_size to safe default, or route subset traffic to baseline model variant; rollback must complete within 30s of trigger.
4) Instrumentation: dashboards + alert rules for p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate, cpu/gpu utilization, queue length, and effective tokens/sec; anomalies must be visible and feed the runbook.
5) Demonstrated cost reduction >= 10% on at least two representative production routes in closed beta while meeting SLOs.

Design proposal (high level):
1) Autosuggest engine (offline + online): offline analyzes historical traces and synthesizes candidate profiles (batch_size, max_wait_ms, max_concurrency_per_shard, enable_prefix_cache, kv_cache_ttl). Online component refines profile using short-running shadow tests.
2) Shadow testing: route mirrored requests to a subset of runtime nodes with the candidate profile but do not affect production responses. Collect latency, queueing, GPU utilization, and model output deltas.
3) Canary orchestration: apply profile to percentage of real traffic with runtime limiters active (see below). Metadata stored in control plane with audit trail.
4) Runtime guardrails / limiters (enforced in router/runtime):
   - Absolute concurrency cap per worker (max inflight requests).
   - Per-route token-rate limiter to avoid sudden bursts interacting badly with large batch windows.
   - Latency-shedder that can preemptively reject or reroute requests when queue depth would violate p99 targets.
   - Cost-safety throttle that bounds the fraction of traffic eligible for aggressive profiles by origin or customer tier.
5) SLO-aware routing: classification of traffic into safe/experimental buckets. Stable/enterprise tenants go to baseline; unknown/low-risk traffic is eligible for optimization. The router can send a fraction of requests matching a fingerprint to the variant.
6) Anomaly detection: timeseries-based monitors (CUSUM + robust trimmed-mean delta) on p95/p99 latency, error-rate, and model divergence score. Also observe resource signals (GPU util, queue length). Detection rules have short-window and medium-window thresholds to avoid chattering.
7) Safe-apply operator: an automated state machine in the control plane that will escalate stages (shadow -> canary 1% -> canary 10% -> scale up) if metrics are stable, and automatically perform rollback actions otherwise.

Rollout & rollback playbook (automated + manual):
- Stage 0 (dev): suggestion + local simulation.
- Stage 1 (shadow): 1 hour shadow run, gather metrics.
- Stage 2 (canary 1%): run 30m; if green, advance.
- Stage 3 (canary 10%): run 1h; if green, expand to 33% then to 100% with staged intervals.
- Automated rollback triggers:
   - p99 latency > baseline_p99 * 1.05 for 5m AND error rate increased by > 50% relative to baseline for 5m.
   - queue length growth > baseline + 4x for 3m.
   - model divergence score > threshold for 10m.
- Automated rollback actions (ordered):
   1) Revert config on variant nodes to baseline (fastest).
   2) Immediately drop batch_size to baseline safe value and disable large-wait.
   3) Route affected traffic to baseline model/region.
   4) Notify oncall and open a rollback incident ticket.

Metrics and instrumentation:
- Per-route: p50/p95/p99 latency, success rate (2xx), error types, tokens/sec, queue length, GPU util, observed batch sizes.
- Delta metrics comparing variant vs baseline (relative latency uplift, cost/unit improvement).
- Rolling window anomaly counters and incident history for audit.
- Dashboards: "Batching Safety - Experimental Runs" and per-route heatmap.

Test plan and validation:
- Synthetic load tests that emulate short-session high-concurrency workloads.
- Replay historical traces in a sandbox using the autosuggest profile.
- Chaos: attach random worker slowdowns and verify automated rollback.
- Canary smoke coverage: validate rollback completes within SLA.

Implementation notes / components to build:
- autosuggest-service (Go): offline profiler + live scoring endpoint.
- shadow-proxy module in runtime: mirror path + metric capture.
- canary-orchestrator in control plane: manifests, audit log, staged rollout logic.
- limiter-enforcement in router: concurrency + token-rate + shedder.
- anomaly-detector (timeseries service): CUSUM + trimmed-mean + adaptive thresholds.
- dashboard + alert rules (Grafana/Prometheus).

Data and privacy considerations:
- Shadow testing uses sampled request payloads (strip PII) and stores hashes for divergence checks.
- Config suggestions tied to route metadata; no user content is stored beyond hashed fingerprints.

Risk and trade-offs:
- Conservative guardrails reduce potential cost wins but lower risk of SLO regressions.
- Detection sensitivity tuning is critical to avoid false positives that block valid savings.
